topics.title: 1.1 Central Angle vs Inscribed Angle Theorem
topics.overview: The central angle subtended by an arc at the center of a circle is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining circumference.
topics.definitions:
$$\angle AOB = 2\angle ACB \quad (\text{Standing on the same arc } AB)$$
$$\angle ADB = \angle ACB \quad (\text{Inscribed angles on the same arc})$$
topics.derivation: In $\triangle OAC$, since $OA = OC = r$, $\triangle OAC$ is isosceles, so $\angle OCA = \angle OAC$. By the exterior angle theorem, the exterior angle at $O$ is $2\angle OCA$. Repeating for $\triangle OBC$ establishes $\angle AOB = 2\angle ACB$.
topics.example: Prove that angles in the same segment of a circle are equal.
topics.pitfalls: In SEE 2-column proofs, always write the exact CDC theorem reason in brackets for every single statement step!

topics.title: 1.1 Fundamental Trigonometric Limits & First Principles
topics.overview: The derivative of a function $f(x)$ represents its instantaneous rate of change and is formally defined through the fundamental limit of a difference quotient as $h \to 0$.
topics.definitions:
$$f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}$$
$$\lim_{\theta \to 0} \frac{\sin\theta}{\theta} = 1 \quad (\theta \text{ in radians})$$
topics.derivation:
To prove $\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x) = \cos x$ by First Principles:
$$f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{\sin(x+h) - \sin x}{h} = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{2\cos\left(x + \frac{h}{2}\right)\sin\left(\frac{h}{2}\right)}{h} = \lim_{h \to 0} \cos\left(x + \frac{h}{2}\right) \cdot \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{\sin(h/2)}{h/2} = \cos x \cdot 1 = \cos x.$$
topics.example: Find the derivative of $f(x) = \sqrt{x}$ from first principles.
topics.pitfalls: When evaluating trigonometric limits from first principles, always verify that the argument inside $\sin$ matches the denominator before applying the standard limit value $1$.

topics.title: 1.1 Fundamental Theorem of Calculus & Standard Antiderivatives
topics.overview: Integration is the analytical inverse of differentiation. For any continuous real function $f(x)$ over an interval $[a, b]$, the definite integral represents the signed area under the curve, defined rigorously by Riemann sums and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
topics.definitions:
$$\int f(x)\,dx = F(x) + C \quad \text{where } F'(x) = f(x)$$
$$\int_{a}^{b} f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a) = \lim_{n \to \infty} \sum_{i=1}^n f(x_i^*)\,\Delta x$$
topics.derivation:
By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: Let $A(x) = \int_a^x f(t)\,dt$. The derivative is given by the definition:
$$A'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{A(x+h) - A(x)}{h} = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{1}{h}\int_x^{x+h} f(t)\,dt = f(x).$$
Hence every continuous function possesses an antiderivative $F(x)$, and any two antiderivatives differ only by an arbitrary constant $C$.
topics.example:
NEB 5-Mark Problem: Evaluate $\int \frac{dx}{x^2 - a^2}$.
Solution: Decomposing into partial fractions:
$$\frac{1}{x^2 - a^2} = \frac{1}{2a}\left(\frac{1}{x - a} - \frac{1}{x + a}\right)$$
Integrating term-by-term yields:
$$\int \frac{dx}{x^2 - a^2} = \frac{1}{2a}\ln\left|\frac{x - a}{x + a}\right| + C.$$
topics.pitfalls: Omitting the arbitrary constant $+ C$ in indefinite integration forfeits the step mark automatically in NEB board evaluation! Always verify whether boundary conditions exist before removing $C$.

topics.title: 2.1 Parabola, Ellipse & Hyperbola Standard Locus Proofs
topics.overview: A conic section is the locus of a point $P(x, y)$ whose distance from a fixed focus $S$ is in constant ratio $e$ (eccentricity) to its perpendicular distance from a directrix line: $SP = e \cdot PM$.
topics.definitions:
$$\text{Ellipse } (e < 1): \frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1, \quad b^2 = a^2(1 - e^2)$$
$$\text{Hyperbola } (e > 1): \frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1, \quad b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1)$$
topics.derivation: Using focus $S(ae, 0)$ and directrix $x = a/e$, locus $SP^2 = e^2 PM^2$ gives $(x - ae)^2 + y^2 = e^2(x - a/e)^2 = (ex - a)^2$. Expanding and collecting terms gives $x^2(1 - e^2) + y^2 = a^2(1 - e^2)$, dividing through yields $\frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$.
topics.example: Find the eccentricity, foci and latus rectum of $9x^2 + 16y^2 = 144$.
topics.pitfalls: Always check whether $a^2 > b^2$ (major axis along x-axis) or $b^2 > a^2$ (major axis along y-axis) before writing foci coordinates!

units.title: Calculus Speed Hacks & Pulchowk Past MCQs

topics.title: 1.1 10-Second Limit & Definite Integral Shortcuts
topics.overview: In IOE CBT exams, combining Maclaurin 3-term series approximations with King's definite integral symmetry evaluates integrals and limits in under 10 seconds.
topics.definitions:
$$\int_a^b \frac{f(x)}{f(x) + f(a+b-x)}\,dx = \frac{b - a}{2}$$
$$\text{Area between } y^2 = 4ax \text{ and } y = mx: \quad A = \frac{8a^2}{3m^3}$$
topics.derivation: Let $I = \int_a^b \frac{f(x)}{f(x)+f(a+b-x)}dx$. Applying property $x \to a+b-x$ gives $I = \int_a^b \frac{f(a+b-x)}{f(a+b-x)+f(x)}dx$. Adding both equations gives $2I = \int_a^b 1\,dx = b - a \implies I = \frac{b-a}{2}$.
topics.example: Evaluate $\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \frac{dx}{1 + \sqrt{\tan x}}$ in 5 seconds. Answer: $(\pi/3 - \pi/6)/2 = \pi/12$.
topics.pitfalls: IOE CBT penalizes $10\%$ ($-0.25$ marks) for incorrect options. Verify whether the function is odd on $[-a, a]$ before guessing!

topics.title: 1.1 Fundamental Trigonometric Limits & First Principles
topics.overview: The derivative of a function $f(x)$ represents its instantaneous rate of change and is formally defined through the fundamental limit of a difference quotient as $h \to 0$.
topics.definitions:
$$f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}$$
$$\lim_{\theta \to 0} \frac{\sin\theta}{\theta} = 1 \quad (\theta \text{ in radians})$$
topics.derivation:
To prove $\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x) = \cos x$ by First Principles:
$$f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{\sin(x+h) - \sin x}{h} = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{2\cos\left(x + \frac{h}{2}\right)\sin\left(\frac{h}{2}\right)}{h} = \lim_{h \to 0} \cos\left(x + \frac{h}{2}\right) \cdot \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{\sin(h/2)}{h/2} = \cos x \cdot 1 = \cos x.$$
topics.example: Find the derivative of $f(x) = \sqrt{x}$ from first principles.
topics.pitfalls: When evaluating trigonometric limits from first principles, always verify that the argument inside $\sin$ matches the denominator before applying the standard limit value $1$.

topics.title: 1.1 Fundamental Theorem of Calculus & Standard Antiderivatives
topics.overview: Integration is the analytical inverse of differentiation. For any continuous real function $f(x)$ over an interval $[a, b]$, the definite integral represents the signed area under the curve, defined rigorously by Riemann sums and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
topics.definitions:
$$\int f(x)\,dx = F(x) + C \quad \text{where } F'(x) = f(x)$$
$$\int_{a}^{b} f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a) = \lim_{n \to \infty} \sum_{i=1}^n f(x_i^*)\,\Delta x$$
topics.derivation:
By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: Let $A(x) = \int_a^x f(t)\,dt$. The derivative is given by the definition:
$$A'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{A(x+h) - A(x)}{h} = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{1}{h}\int_x^{x+h} f(t)\,dt = f(x).$$
Hence every continuous function possesses an antiderivative $F(x)$, and any two antiderivatives differ only by an arbitrary constant $C$.
topics.example:
NEB 5-Mark Problem: Evaluate $\int \frac{dx}{x^2 - a^2}$.
Solution: Decomposing into partial fractions:
$$\frac{1}{x^2 - a^2} = \frac{1}{2a}\left(\frac{1}{x - a} - \frac{1}{x + a}\right)$$
Integrating term-by-term yields:
$$\int \frac{dx}{x^2 - a^2} = \frac{1}{2a}\ln\left|\frac{x - a}{x + a}\right| + C.$$
topics.pitfalls: Omitting the arbitrary constant $+ C$ in indefinite integration forfeits the step mark automatically in NEB board evaluation! Always verify whether boundary conditions exist before removing $C$.

topics.title: 2.1 Parabola, Ellipse & Hyperbola Standard Locus Proofs
topics.overview: A conic section is the locus of a point $P(x, y)$ whose distance from a fixed focus $S$ is in constant ratio $e$ (eccentricity) to its perpendicular distance from a directrix line: $SP = e \cdot PM$.
topics.definitions:
$$\text{Ellipse } (e < 1): \frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1, \quad b^2 = a^2(1 - e^2)$$
$$\text{Hyperbola } (e > 1): \frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1, \quad b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1)$$
topics.derivation: Using focus $S(ae, 0)$ and directrix $x = a/e$, locus $SP^2 = e^2 PM^2$ gives $(x - ae)^2 + y^2 = e^2(x - a/e)^2 = (ex - a)^2$. Expanding and collecting terms gives $x^2(1 - e^2) + y^2 = a^2(1 - e^2)$, dividing through yields $\frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$.
topics.example: Find the eccentricity, foci and latus rectum of $9x^2 + 16y^2 = 144$.
topics.pitfalls: Always check whether $a^2 > b^2$ (major axis along x-axis) or $b^2 > a^2$ (major axis along y-axis) before writing foci coordinates!

units.title: Calculus Speed Hacks & Pulchowk Past MCQs

topics.title: 1.1 10-Second Limit & Definite Integral Shortcuts
topics.overview: In IOE CBT exams, combining Maclaurin 3-term series approximations with King's definite integral symmetry evaluates integrals and limits in under 10 seconds.
topics.definitions:
$$\int_a^b \frac{f(x)}{f(x) + f(a+b-x)}\,dx = \frac{b - a}{2}$$
$$\text{Area between } y^2 = 4ax \text{ and } y = mx: \quad A = \frac{8a^2}{3m^3}$$
topics.derivation: Let $I = \int_a^b \frac{f(x)}{f(x)+f(a+b-x)}dx$. Applying property $x \to a+b-x$ gives $I = \int_a^b \frac{f(a+b-x)}{f(a+b-x)+f(x)}dx$. Adding both equations gives $2I = \int_a^b 1\,dx = b - a \implies I = \frac{b-a}{2}$.
topics.example: Evaluate $\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \frac{dx}{1 + \sqrt{\tan x}}$ in 5 seconds. Answer: $(\pi/3 - \pi/6)/2 = \pi/12$.
topics.pitfalls: IOE CBT penalizes $10\%$ ($-0.25$ marks) for incorrect options. Verify whether the function is odd on $[-a, a]$ before guessing!
